chunks: And from him, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī al-Washshāʾ; and al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ, who said:
Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام said to me: “Repetition is in the first two rakʿahs, and forgetfulness is in the last two rakʿahs.”

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّل: Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام, the authority conveying the ruling
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ: the last two units of the salat (prayer)
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَوَّلَتَيْنِ: the first two units of the salat (prayer)
key_terms.السَّهْوُ: forgetfulness or inadvertent error in salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْإِعَادَةُ: repetition of the salat (prayer) or portion due to error

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on forgetfulness in the first two and last two rakʿahs of salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding forgetfulness in salat (prayer). It distinguishes between the first two rakʿahs and the last two rakʿahs, indicating that error in the first two entails repetition, while forgetfulness in the last two is treated under the rules of sahw.
